comment: Don't swallow a broad `except Exception` silently — if `call_external_service` fails, `result` is never assigned and this will NameError somewhere worse, or (if it were pre-assigned) silently return stale/wrong data. Either catch the specific exception you expect and handle it, or let it propagate.

This looks like a live API key committed in source. Pull it from an environment variable (or the secret store we already use for GEMINI_API_KEY) and rotate this key — it's now in git history even if removed in the next commit.

This calls Gemini with no fallback path — if the API is down, rate-limited, or there's no cassette in CI, this throws and blocks the caller. Every AI call in this repo needs a `GeminiUnavailable` except branch with a safe deterministic default, same as `ai/routing/decide.py`.

diff_hunk:
query = f"SELECT * FROM ideas WHERE text LIKE '%{search_term}%'"
db.execute(query)
comment: User-controlled `search_term` is interpolated directly into SQL — classic injection risk. Use a parameterized query (SQLAlchemy's `text()` with bound params, or the ORM query builder) instead of an f-string.

New public function with no docstring — at minimum say what the time window means and what gets returned when there's no evidence. Someone calling this from a new pipeline step shouldn't have to read the body to find out.

diff_hunk:
def handle_request(req):
    # parses input
    # validates auth
    # queries db
    # calls external api
    # formats response
    # logs metrics
    ...120 lines...
comment: This function does six unrelated things in one body — hard to review as a single diff and hard to unit test in isolation. Split into named helpers (parse/validate/fetch/format) even if each is only called once; makes the next PR's diff against this much smaller too.

Leftover debug print — this runs on every request in prod and will flood stdout/logs. Remove it, or if you need this visibility use the structured logger (`logging.getLogger(...)`) at DEBUG level so it can be toggled off.

`verify=False` disables TLS certificate verification for this client — any MITM on this network path can intercept or tamper with the response. If this is a self-signed cert in a dev cluster, pin the CA instead of disabling verification entirely.
